snippet.title: Pepsi Once Controlled A Navy? #shorts #pepsi
snippet.description:
Pepsi Once Controlled A Navy? 

During the Cold War, the Soviet Union didn’t have US dollars to pay Pepsi. But Pepsi wanted to enter the USSR market at any cost. So instead of money, the Soviet Union paid Pepsi with decommissioned submarines, warships, cruisers, and destroyers.

At one point, Pepsi officially owned 17 submarines, a cruiser, and multiple warships, making it technically one of the most powerful organizations on Earth — even stronger than many countries’ navies.

Of course, Pepsi wasn’t going to start a military force. The company later scrapped all the ships, but this moment remains one of the most shocking untold brand stories in history.

snippet.title: How Videocon Destroyed Itself!
snippet.description:
How Videocon Destroyed Itself! Aman Sharma
In 1986, Venugopal Dhoot spotted a golden opportunity. As Doordarshan started color broadcasting, India’s middle class wanted color TVs—but couldn’t afford expensive ones. That’s when Videocon entered the market with affordable televisions and quickly took over Indian homes.

Success followed fast. Videocon expanded into ACs, washing machines, refrigerators, and music systems, and revenue soared.
But with success came overconfidence.

Believing they could win anywhere, Videocon invested billions into oil & gas, power, and telecom—industries they barely understood. Then came the 2012 2G Spectrum scam, where the Supreme Court cancelled their telecom license, causing massive losses.

At the same time, the electronics market was changing rapidly. LED and LCD TVs replaced bulky CRT TVs, but Videocon failed to adapt. To survive, the company took a ₹3,250 crore loan from ICICI Bank, which later exposed a major corruption scandal involving the bank’s CEO.

With funding blocked and losses piling up, Videocon collapsed under ₹90,000 crore of debt by 2018.

This is the story of how wrong bets, slow adaptation, and unchecked ambition destroyed one of India’s biggest consumer brands.

snippet.title: Pablo Escobar’s Rise & Fall | The Godfather of Cocaine (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
An investigation into the bloody rise and fall of Pablo Escobar and how the empire he built set the stage for the modern narco-trafficking industry. (Aired 1995)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

This archival FRONTLINE documentary examines how one drug, cocaine, began flowing into the U.S. at an industrial scale in the 1970s and 1980s — and the pivotal role of the notorious Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar, the boss of the Medellin cocaine cartel. 

With remarkable access to Escobar’s family, relatives of his victims, and both Colombian and U.S. officials, “The Godfather of Cocaine” traces how Escobar built a multi-billion-dollar fortune through international cocaine smuggling alliances and a sophisticated operation to traffic cocaine into the U.S.

Escobar maintained his dominance through violent repression and extreme brutality, with his cartel funneling drug profits into attacks and killings that brought Colombia to a state of virtual civil war. 

Colombian police and the U.S. DEA hunted Escobar down and assassinated him in 1993, but it didn’t end the narco-trafficking model he built. 

“The death of Escobar was a landmark in the history of an industry, but it wasn't a victory, in the sense that it didn’t put anything out of business,” Senate investigator Jack Blum said in the documentary. “It didn't change the pace of trafficking. It didn't raise or lower the price of cocaine.”

“The Godfather of Cocaine” was produced by William Cran and Stephanie Tepper. The associate producers were Christopher Buchanan and Marcela Gaviria. The documentary was written and directed by William Cran. Cran, a prolific and acclaimed documentary filmmaker, passed away in 2025: https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/article/remembering-william-cran-prolific-and-acclaimed-documentary-filmmaker/

snippet.title: This Is How Balaji Wafers Destroyed Lay’s! Aman Sharma
snippet.description:
This Is How Balaji Wafers Destroyed Lay’s! Aman Sharma
Lay’s dominated India’s chips market, but one Indian brand noticed a critical flaw — too much air, too few chips.
For middle-class consumers, Lay’s simply didn’t feel like value for money.

Instead of burning money on advertising, Balaji Wafers invested in quantity — giving 30–40% more chips in every packet.
That single move shifted the entire middle-class market toward Balaji.

Then came the masterstroke:
Balaji openly mocked low-quantity chips with its iconic slogan —
“Hawa Kam, Wafer Zyada.”

Understanding India’s diversity, Balaji launched state-specific flavours —
Gathiya for Gujarat, Chat Chaska for Maharashtra, extra spicy wafers for Rajasthan.
Later, they expanded into bhujia, bhel, traditional snacks, and even western snacks like nachos, pop rings, and noodles to attract the youth.

Today, these strategies have turned Balaji Wafers into a ₹5,000 crore annual business, proving that value beats hype — even against global giants.

Vijay was once brutally mocked after his first lead film failed in 1992. Media even called him “rat-faced.” But instead of giving up, he kept working relentlessly and delivered back-to-back blockbusters, eventually becoming Tamil cinema’s beloved “Thalapathy.”

But his biggest challenge began in 2024, when he launched his political party, TVK, in a state dominated by powerful parties for over 60 years.

Just before elections, tragedy struck when a stampede at one of his rallies killed 41 people. Everyone believed his political career was over.

But unlike most politicians, Vijay publicly accepted responsibility and personally helped the affected families. That honesty changed public perception — and eventually helped him rise to become Tamil Nadu’s CM.

This is the story of how insults, failures, and one difficult decision transformed an actor into a leader.

snippet.title: Waymo vs Tesla Self Driving: Why Elon Musk Is LOSING?
snippet.description:
Waymo vs. Tesla: The REAL Truth About the Driverless Taxi Race! (2025 Update) | Waymo Self Driving Car | Waymo Car | Waymo Taxi | Waymo Driverless Car | Waymo vs Tesla | Waymo Robotaxi | Waymo San Francisco | Tesla FSD | Tesla FSD accident | Waymo vs Tesla | Lidar | Who's Winning | Self Driving Race | Cybercab 

Is Elon Musk WRONG about driverless tech? While Tesla's FSD promises have stretched for a decade (since 2014!), Google's Waymo is already DOMINATING the driverless taxi market. In this video, we break down why Waymo is leading the autonomous vehicle revolution and why Tesla is struggling to keep up.

Timestamps:

00:00 Intro
00:37 Waymo vs Tesla FSD
01:12 Elon's Timeline Issue
02:56 Lidar vs Elon
05:16 Elon's Hypocrisy 
06:25 REAL TRUTH
09:05 We Robot Event

Waymo is WINNING:
Waymo's fleet of fully autonomous (Level 4) robotaxis isn't a future dream – it's a present REALITY. Successfully operating in Phoenix, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Austin, Waymo provides a staggering 250,000 paid rides PER WEEK (as of April 2025, CNBC). With expansion plans for Atlanta and Miami, Waymo is tangible proof of successful autonomous mobility.

Tesla's Lag & Broken Promises:
Despite Elon Musk's relentless hype since 2014, Tesla remains stuck at Level 2 autonomy, requiring constant human supervision. The much-anticipated Full Self-Driving (FSD) has faced endless postponements. Musk's latest promise from the October 2024 "We, Robot" event? A Waymo-competing Cybercab by 2027. Given the track record, skepticism is warranted.

The LIDAR Debate: Musk's Flawed Critique of Waymo
Elon Musk's main attack on Waymo centers on its use of LIDAR, a sophisticated 3D mapping tech crucial for safety, especially in low-light, adverse weather, and complex urban environments where Tesla's camera-only system falters. Musk claims LIDAR is too expensive and not scalable.

Here's why Elon is WRONG about LIDAR:

1️⃣ Safety FIRST, Not Cost: Waymo's LIDAR-equipped fleet has an exceptional safety record, linked to only ONE fatality. In stark contrast, Tesla’s Autopilot and FSD systems have been associated with 51 DEATHS. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has even criticized Tesla’s "inadequate" safety measures. Safety should ALWAYS be the priority over cost in autonomous driving.

2️⃣ LIDAR Costs are PLUMMETING: Musk's "high cost" argument is outdated. LIDAR prices have nosedived by ~90% since 2015. From $75,000 in 2009-2011, units dropped to $7,500 by 2017 (Innoviz, March 2025). In 2025, reports suggest costs could be as low as $1,000, dismantling Musk's core criticism.

3️⃣ Elon's Double Standard: Musk dismisses Waymo's LIDAR due to cost, yet Tesla's entire product line (EVs, Cybertruck) is premium-priced. If Waymo is "flawed" for using expensive LIDAR, is Tesla "flawed" because BYD produces significantly cheaper EVs? Without hefty U.S. tariffs on Chinese EVs, BYD could easily challenge Tesla. This reveals a narrative driven by competition, not principle.

Key Takeaways:

Tesla: 51 fatalities (Autopilot/FSD). Waymo: 1 fatality (LIDAR).

LIDAR cost in 2025: Potentially under $1,000.

Musk's Pattern of Narrative Control:

Elon's attacks on Waymo mirror his tactics against other competitors like OpenAI. When Sam Altman and ChatGPT gained prominence, Musk criticized OpenAI's shift to a for-profit model, despite evidence he himself explored a for-profit structure for OpenAI (and xAI is neither open-source nor non-profit). He accused Google’s Larry Page of not taking AI safety seriously, yet when Waymo prioritizes safety with LIDAR, Musk shifts the goalpost to cost. This isn't about industry progress; it's about image and damaging rivals.

Ego, Envy, or Strategy?

Despite his past achievements with EVs and SpaceX, Elon Musk often displays jealousy and insecurity towards competitors. He’s not just an entrepreneur but a skilled narrative manipulator.

"We, Robot" Event: More Hype Than Substance

The October 2024 "We, Robot" event, showcasing the Cybercab, was a marketing spectacle to counter Waymo's dominance, lacking concrete timelines or technical roadmaps. Classic Musk overpromise.

The Real Race:

The driverless taxi race isn't about the cheapest system or the most hype. It's about the **SAFEST, most RELIABLE one.** Right now, Waymo is unequivocally winning. Tesla has a mountain to climb.

snippet.title: Examining U.S.-Saudi Ties | The Crown Prince & the President (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
Martin Smith examines the alliance between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and President Donald Trump in this 90-minute documentary. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

What is behind the alliance between President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS), and what are the ramifications for the U.S., Saudi Arabia and the Middle East as a whole? 

Answers unfold in “The Crown Prince & the President,” the latest documentary from an award-winning team that includes directors, writers and producers Martin Smith and Marcela Gaviria, and co-producers Scott Anger and Jennifer Brooks. 
 
“‘The Crown Prince & the President’ is based on over 100 interviews I have done in the U.S. and abroad,” says Smith, who also serves as correspondent and has covered the U.S.-Saudi relationship for more than 20 years. “Our investigation is an incisive look at the forces binding the two men and their countries together, and what each stands to gain — from ambitions for a new Middle East, to arms deals, investments and personal profit.”
 
Over the course of the documentary, that story is told with insights from former U.S. officials and diplomats, members of the Saudi government, Trump administration insiders, Saudi dissidents, human rights and foreign policy experts, and journalists who have covered financial ties between the Trump family and Saudi Arabia. 
 
What emerges is a sharp chronicle of how the alliance between the crown prince who promised reform and the Trump administration has grown, despite MBS’ crackdown on dissent and the murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi, in which MBS denied involvement.
 
The documentary also offers a powerful examination of the Trump administration’s foreign policy strategy for Saudi Arabia, and the implications for the surrounding region, the U.S. and the world.
 
“The Crown Prince & the President” is a FRONTLINE production with Rain Media. The correspondent is Martin Smith. The co-producers are Scott Anger and Jennifer Brooks. The writers, producers and directors are Marcela Gaviria & Martin Smith. The managing editor of FRONTLINE is Andrew Metz. The editor-in-chief and executive producer of FRONTLINE is Raney Aronson-Rath.

snippet.title: For-Profit Adoptions & Misconduct Allegations (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS) + Retro Report
snippet.description:
With Retro Report, an investigation into how so-called “baby brokers” have targeted pregnant women and families looking to adopt, and an epicenter of the problem in Utah.

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

The adoption industry in the U.S. is a multi-billion-dollar business, where demand outpaces the number of infants available for adoption. In “Baby Brokers,” FRONTLINE and Retro Report investigate a loosely-regulated corner of the industry described as “adoption tourism” and examine how allegations of misconduct involving for-profit agencies and brokers have mounted. 

The documentary illuminates a patchwork system, where allegations of misconduct have stacked up in states like Utah with historically more permissive laws. 

In the documentary, the head of an adoption agency in Utah says that out-of-state adoptions fulfill an important need. But other sources express concern about how brokers and agencies have used cash and housing offers as incentives for vulnerable women in other states.

In recent months, Utah has moved to tighten some of its laws in response to mounting criticisms from birth mothers, their advocates, and adoptive parents. And at the federal level, lawmakers from a number of states are backing a bipartisan bill aimed at reining in unlicensed brokers who funnel pregnant women and families across state lines for adoptions.

As the debate over “adoption tourism” continues, “Baby Brokers” is a must-watch exploration of the practice, the role of brokers, and the impact on both birth mothers and adoptive parents.
